criteria.text: The participant has a histologically-confirmed diagnosis of stage IV non-squamous or squamous NSCLC.
The participant has measurable disease based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1 within one month of first vaccine.
Target lesions situated in a previously irradiated area are considered measurable if progression has been demonstrated in such lesions.
The participant has completed 3-4 cycles of chemoimmunotherapy, without evidence of progressive disease.
Pembrolizumab has to be included in at least 3 of these cycles.
The participant has not received more than 2 cycles of maintenance pembrolizumab and/or pemetrexed and is a candidate for continuation of this therapy.
The participant has at least 1 site of disease that could be biopsied during treatment.
The site to be biopsied should not be a site that is used to determine measurable disease for efficacy purposes.
Lesions that will be biopsied should not be on a previously irradiated area unless progression has been demonstrated in such lesions.

The participant is at least 28 days post systemic steroids prior to enrollment, unless this is a steroid administered concurrently with chemotherapy or used as part of prophylaxis to prevent intravenous (IV) contrast reactions.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status Score of 0 or 1.

The participant has recovered from major infections and/or surgical procedures, and in the opinion of a principle investigator (PI)/co-PI/study physician/physician extender, does not have any significant active concurrent medical illnesses precluding protocol treatment.
The participant is willing to undergo up to two serial biopsies while on study.
The participant has an estimated life expectancy of more than 6 months.
White blood cells (WBC) >= 3000/mm^3 (within 60 days of first vaccination).
Lymphocyte count >= 800/mm^3 (within 60 days of first vaccination).
Platelet count >= 75,000/mm^3 (within 60 days of first vaccination).
Hemoglobin (Hgb) >= 9 g/dl (within 60 days of first vaccination).
Serum creatinine =< 1.2 mg/dl or creatinine clearance > 50 ml/min (within 60 days of first vaccination).
Total bilirubin =< 1.5 mg/dl (within 60 days of first vaccination).

Aspartate aminotransferase/serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (AST/SGOT) =< 2 times upper limit of normal (ULN) or SGOT =< 5 times upper limit of normal (ULN) in the presence of liver metastasis (within 60 days of first vaccination).
If female of childbearing potential has a negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to receiving the first dose of study medication.
All patients who are having sex that can lead to pregnancy must agree to contraception for the duration of study.
The participant is at least 18 years of age.

The participant has any of the following cardiac conditions: Symptomatic restrictive cardiomyopathy, Unstable angina within 4 months prior to enrollment, New York Heart Association functional class III-IV heart failure on active treatment, Symptomatic pericardial effusion.
The participant has central nervous system (CNS) metastasis that have not been treated.

The participant has previously treated brain metastases and is clinically stable for at least 4 weeks, has no evidence of new or enlarging brain metastases, and is off steroids for 2 weeks prior to dosing with study medication.
The participant has any contraindication to receiving recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor (rhuGM-CSF) based products.
The participant has any clinically significant autoimmune disease that requires active treatment with immunosuppressants.

The participant has a known history of another prior invasive malignancy within 2 years, except subjects with early stage cancer that has undergone potentially curative therapy with no evidence of that disease recurrence for 2 years since initiation of that therapy.
The participant is simultaneously enrolled in any other treatment study.
The participant is pregnant or breastfeeding.

The participant has genetic driver alterations (e.g EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET ex 14, RET) for which targeted treatment exist and are Food and Drug Association (FDA) approved, except if the subject is not eligible or has progressed through those therapies.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Multiple Antigen Vaccine (STEMVAC) for the Treatment of Patients With Stage IV Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". Your earlier answers already covered 7 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you completed 3 to 4 cycles of chemoimmunotherapy? Also, have you been told that your disease has not progressed (grown or spread) since starting treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I had the Tecentriq immune one and it stopped working, the cancer grew. So I guess that means it progressed? I don't know about cycles of chemoimmunotherapy specifically.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. Do you know if the drug pembrolizumab was included in at least 3 of your treatment cycles?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, honey. I only remember having Tecentriq, the immune one. I'm not sure if that was pembrolizumab or what else was in the mix.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if you received more than 2 cycles of maintenance treatment with pembrolizumab or pemetrexed? (Pemetrexed is a chemo drug often given with pembrolizumab.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, honey. I only remember having Tecentriq, the immune one. I'm not sure about pemetrexed or how many cycles of maintenance I had.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, did you receive more than 2 cycles of maintenance treatment with pembrolizumab or pemetrexed? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, honey. I only remember having Tecentriq, the immune one. I'm not sure about pemetrexed or how many cycles of maintenance I had.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if there is at least one spot of cancer that a doctor could take a small tissue sample from (biopsy) during the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I wouldn't know that. I'm not sure if they can take a biopsy from my spots or not.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if the spot your doctor plans to biopsy is the same one they use to measure how the cancer is responding to treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I wouldn't know that. I'm not sure if the spot they'd biopsy is the same one they use to measure things.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if the spot planned for biopsy has ever been treated with radiation?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No radiation. I haven't had any radiation at all, not to the chest or anywhere else.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you taken any systemic steroids in the last 28 days? (This includes pills, injections, or IVs, but not inhalers or eye drops.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I take a little white pill in the morning, I'm not sure what it is. I don't know if it's a steroid or how much I'm taking.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any major infections or surgeries in the last 28 days, or do you have any other significant health conditions right now?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know about infections or surgeries in the last 28 days. I'm just up and about, though I can't do the heavy cleaning anymore. I don't know if that counts as a significant health condition.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to undergo up to two additional biopsies while participating in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know, honey. I'm not sure if I can handle two more biopsies. I'm just up and about, but I can't do the heavy cleaning anymore.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, are you willing to have up to two extra biopsies during the study, or would you prefer not to?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know, honey. I'm not sure if I can handle two more biopsies. I'm just up and about, but I can't do the heavy cleaning anymore.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Your doctor has estimated that you have more than 6 months to live, correct? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know, honey. I'm not sure how long the doctor thinks I have left. I just know I'm up and about, but I can't do the heavy cleaning anymore.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant, or do you think there is any chance you could be pregnant?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh heavens, no. I'm 67 and retired, so that's certainly not the case.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Just to confirm, are you at least 18 years old?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh yes, I'm 67, so I'm certainly old enough! I'm well past 18.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any of these heart conditions: symptomatic restrictive cardiomyopathy, unstable angina in the last 4 months, severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV), or symptomatic pericardial effusion? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any of those heart problems. My heart is fine, thank the Lord.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with brain metastases? If so, have you been stable for at least 4 weeks with no new or enlarging spots, and have you stopped taking steroids for at least 2 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, they checked my brain and it's fine, thank the Lord. So I haven't had any brain metastases.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently enrolled in any other treatment study or clinical trial?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm not in any other studies right now. I'm just focusing on this one trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told you have genetic changes in your cancer, such as EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET, or RET, for which there are FDA-approved targeted treatments?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I wouldn't know that, honey. I've never been told about any of those genetic changes like EGFR or ALK. You'd have to ask my doctor about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you aren't sure, would it be okay if I asked your doctor to check your medical records for any known genetic changes in your cancer, such as EGFR, ALK, or ROS1?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, that sounds fine, honey. If the doctor can check the records for me, that would be a big help. I really don't know those things myself.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
